evidence: Every merged source file equals one parent exactly: diffing the staged tree against 43ab360 lists only HEAD-side files (SavedLocationsScreen, SavedLocationManager, MainActivity, manifest, gradle) and diffing against b661327 lists only branch-side files, so no file received hand-merged conflict edits; the build evidence written after the sources reports BUILD SUCCESSFUL with all 35 tasks executed.
NON_CV_CLOSE_DELAY_MS is declared once as 200L at PicapOfferCloser.kt line 15 and consumed at line 57, and no 500 ms close delay exists anywhere under app sources.

SavedLocationsScreen export null-checks the stream and catches Exception, import uses a null-safe read and catches Throwable, and the merge left that file byte-identical to b661327; the shell onDestroy still hides the overlay, cancels serviceScope and dismisses the popup, and PicapParser.parseOrder bounds-checks every index access.

findings.claim: Substituting a missing WhatsApp pickup km with the 999.0 sentinel makes condition 3 accept when the km switch is on and the threshold is at or above 5.0, where the accf641 base required a parsed km in that clause. This is a silent auto-accept policy relaxation rather than a crash path, and the identical code ships on 43ab360.
proof_refs: WhatsAppResponder.kt line 136 passes kmRecogida or the fallback 999.0 into evaluateAutoAccept, and NotificationInterceptorService.kt line 162 does the same for notification text.

AutoAcceptEvaluator.kt line 66 returns accepted when isKmEnabled is true and maxKm is greater than or equal to 5.0 without reading km, while the accf641 NotificationInterceptorService third clause required kmRecogida not null.
The diff between accf641 and 43ab360 shows both call sites already present on the refactor branch, so no merge-introduced change.

findings.claim: The scanned id guard is a read-then-contains check inside a Dispatchers.Default coroutine while NotificationInterceptorService adds ids on the main thread, and addScannedWhatsAppServiceId performs a non-atomic read-modify-write of the StateFlow value, so both paths can pass the guard and duplicate the reply for one service. The same structure exists in both parents, so no new TOCTOU was created by the merge.
proof_refs: WhatsAppResponder.kt reads scannedWhatsAppServiceIds.value at line 109 and adds the id at line 118 inside a coroutine launched on the default dispatcher.
OrderStateManager.addScannedWhatsAppServiceId assigns the flow value from a fresh read of that same value, which is not an atomic update.
The accf641 MyAccessibilityService processWhatsAppText block contains the same contains then add sequence and the same notification listener add, so the race predates the merge.

findings.claim: onDestroy cancels serviceScope but never removes the main-looper posts that schedule the delayed auto-accept and the send retry, so those runnables can execute after teardown against a destroyed service instance and its stale closures. The same posts exist at accf641, so this is a pre-existing gap rather than something the split introduced.
proof_refs: MyAccessibilityService.onDestroy runs hideKmOverlay, serviceScope.cancel, floatingPopup dismiss and instance null, with no Handler removal.
WhatsAppResponder.kt posts the delayed accept at line 150 and the send retry at line 275 to a main looper Handler that outlives the scope.
The accf641 MyAccessibilityService WhatsApp block contains the same postDelayed calls, confirming the behavior is unchanged by the merge.
